annotation.kind: source selection, tier label, operational multidimensional complex FFT family, and uniform asymptotic formalization of Theorem 2(a)

assumptions: The number of dimensions is positive, every coordinate length is positive, and each coordinate has a certified one-dimensional mixed-radix FFT plan.
The plan, common gamma, and input are fixed before positive epsilon varies; every run uses a Wilkinson model whose epsilon field is that varying parameter and whose gamma field is the fixed gamma.
The input is exactly represented, as section 6 states for the preceding roundoff analysis, and the execution applies T_m first and T_1 last.
Every computed coordinate state is generated by the operational rounded mixed-radix roots, products, and sums; local errors are differences derived from those states rather than supplied data.

Every per-axis estimate is derived from the operational scalar Wilkinson model, the generated one-dimensional mixed-radix trace on each fiber, Theorem 1's operation-level analysis, and equation (4.4)'s exact prefix scaling; no local-error bound is supplied by the caller.
The scalar operations satisfy the Wilkinson model, with no separate exceptional-value semantics.
The exact output RMS is positive so that the paper's printed relative-error ratio is defined.

conditions.L: The identical fixed statement and P09 shared files are present; the frozen NumStability library is also present.
conditions.N: The fixed statement and P09 shared files are present; no NumStability artifact is present.

formal_statement.lean_header: theorem p09_t3_multidimensional_rms_error_bound {m : Nat} [NeZero m] (plan : P09MultidimensionalFftPlan m) (gamma : Real) (family : P09AsymptoticMultidimensionalFftFamily plan gamma) (hexactOutput : 0 < p09MultiRms (p09FamilyMultiExactOutput family)) : exists C : Real, 0 <= C and exists radius : Real, 0 < radius and forall epsilon : P09PositiveEpsilon, epsilon.1 <= radius -> p09MultiRms (p09FamilyMultiFftRoundoffError family epsilon) / p09MultiRms (p09FamilyMultiExactOutput family) <= epsilon.1 * (sum i, p09AxisK (plan.axis i) gamma) + C * epsilon.1^2
formal_statement.plain_language: For one fixed multidimensional FFT plan, exactly represented input, and gamma, the linked operational runs satisfy Theorem 2(a)'s relative RMS bound uniformly for all sufficiently small positive epsilon, with first-order coefficient sum_l K(N_l,gamma) and one epsilon-independent second-order coefficient.

informal_proof: Derive each local error and the telescoping recurrence from the generated coordinate states. Extend the complex Euclidean triangle inequality to the finite propagated errors, bound each computed intermediate RMS from that recurrence, sum the uniform equation (4.3)-(4.4) estimates, choose a sufficiently small common radius, absorb only products of two first-order terms into one uniform epsilon-squared coefficient, and divide by the positive fixed exact-output RMS.
informal_statement: Theorem 2(a)'s relative RMS estimate for a fixed linked multidimensional complex FFT family, with operational coordinate executions, exact input representation, fixed one-dimensional K constants, and uniform right-neighborhood O(epsilon squared) semantics.

review_record_not_for_run_prompt.note: The frozen MatrixAlgebra object supplies vecNorm2_le_of_abs_le and vecNorm2_add_le, which the condition-L proof combines to obtain the complex-array triangle step. The proof then extends that step through the generated nested trace, derives finite telescoping and intermediate-state bounds, solves the uniform error recurrence, and discharges the asymptotic quantifiers. No mounted theorem states this linked multidimensional result.
